title: Lymphoid System and Immunity — Curated Lecture Figures
description: Manually selected anatomical-model photographs, labeled anatomical illustrations, histology, and physiological/immunological diagrams from the two Chapter 22 lecture decks.
selectionMethod: Manual review of all 71 slides; image-based teaching value prioritized, repeated figures and text-only slides omitted. Some panels combined into a single study figure.

items.title: Lymph node: labeled internal structure
items.description: Afferent and efferent lymphatic vessels, capsule, subcapsular sinus, cortex, paracortex, medullary cords, sinuses, blood vessels, and hilum.
items.alt: Afferent and efferent lymphatic vessels, capsule, subcapsular sinus, cortex, paracortex, medullary cords, sinuses, blood vessels, and hilum.

items.title: Tonsils: locations in the pharynx
items.description: Sagittal head illustration identifying pharyngeal, palatine, and lingual tonsillar tissue around the entrance to the upper aerodigestive tract.
items.alt: Sagittal head illustration identifying pharyngeal, palatine, and lingual tonsillar tissue around the entrance to the upper aerodigestive tract.

items.title: Spleen: visceral surface and hilum
items.description: Surface anatomy of the spleen with the hilum, splenic artery and vein, and its relations to adjacent organs.
items.alt: Surface anatomy of the spleen with the hilum, splenic artery and vein, and its relations to adjacent organs.

items.title: Spleen on a classroom teaching model
items.description: Photograph of an anatomical classroom model showing the spleen adjacent to the stomach and pancreas, with the splenic vessels and hilum labeled on the slide.
items.alt: Photograph of an anatomical classroom model showing the spleen adjacent to the stomach and pancreas, with the splenic vessels and hilum labeled on the slide.

items.title: Thymus: gross anatomical landmarks
items.description: Bilateral thymic lobes, septa, and lobules labeled in a gross anatomical drawing.
items.alt: Bilateral thymic lobes, septa, and lobules labeled in a gross anatomical drawing.

items.title: Peyer’s patches and mucosal lymphoid tissue
items.description: Intestinal mucosa cross-section showing aggregated lymphoid nodules (Peyer’s patches) beneath the epithelial surface.
items.alt: Intestinal mucosa cross-section showing aggregated lymphoid nodules (Peyer’s patches) beneath the epithelial surface.

items.title: Intestinal lipid absorption and lymph transport
items.description: Lecture figure connecting absorbed lipids and chylomicrons to lymphatic transport and later lipoprotein metabolism.
items.alt: Lecture figure connecting absorbed lipids and chylomicrons to lymphatic transport and later lipoprotein metabolism.
items.scienceReview: The slide emphasizes lipoprotein metabolism; interpret it alongside the course explanation of lacteals and lymph transport.

items.title: Lymphoid system: whole-body anatomy
items.description: Overview of lymphatic vessels, nodes, tonsils, thymus, spleen, appendix, and mucosa-associated lymphoid tissues in anatomical position.
items.alt: Overview of lymphatic vessels, nodes, tonsils, thymus, spleen, appendix, and mucosa-associated lymphoid tissues in anatomical position.

items.title: Blood capillaries versus lymphatic capillaries
items.description: A tissue-level illustration distinguishing the branching blood capillary network from blind-ended lymphatic capillaries and showing interstitial fluid movement.
items.alt: A tissue-level illustration distinguishing the branching blood capillary network from blind-ended lymphatic capillaries and showing interstitial fluid movement.

items.title: Lymphatic capillary: one-way fluid entry
items.description: Magnified depiction of blind-ended lymphatic channels, overlapping endothelial edges, and movement of interstitial fluid into lymph.
items.alt: Magnified depiction of blind-ended lymphatic channels, overlapping endothelial edges, and movement of interstitial fluid into lymph.

items.title: Collecting lymphatic vessels and neighboring blood vessels
items.description: Lymphatic collectors alongside an artery and vein, including valve placement and anatomical cross-sections.
items.alt: Lymphatic collectors alongside an artery and vein, including valve placement and anatomical cross-sections.

items.title: Lymphatic valves: light microscopy
items.description: Light-microscopy specimen showing valves in a lymphatic vessel; complements the vessel schematic.
items.alt: Light-microscopy specimen showing valves in a lymphatic vessel; complements the vessel schematic.

items.title: Right lymphatic duct versus thoracic duct territories
items.description: Body-territory map distinguishing the upper right region typically drained by the right lymphatic duct from the much larger thoracic duct drainage region.
items.alt: Body-territory map distinguishing the upper right region typically drained by the right lymphatic duct from the much larger thoracic duct drainage region.

items.title: Major lymphatic trunks and thoracic duct
items.description: Detailed labeled thoracic illustration with jugular, subclavian, bronchomediastinal, lumbar and intestinal trunks, cisterna chyli, and venous junctions.
items.alt: Detailed labeled thoracic illustration with jugular, subclavian, bronchomediastinal, lumbar and intestinal trunks, cisterna chyli, and venous junctions.

items.title: Lymphocytes in a peripheral blood smear
items.description: A blood-smear photograph illustrating the round dark nuclei and peripheral cytoplasm of circulating lymphocytes among erythrocytes.
items.alt: A blood-smear photograph illustrating the round dark nuclei and peripheral cytoplasm of circulating lymphocytes among erythrocytes.

items.title: Lymphopoiesis: B, T, and NK cell lineages
items.description: Developmental scheme relating red bone marrow and the thymus to B-cell, T-cell, and natural killer cell lineages.
items.alt: Developmental scheme relating red bone marrow and the thymus to B-cell, T-cell, and natural killer cell lineages.
items.scienceReview: A simplified teaching lineage diagram; modern developmental pathways and maturation signals are more nuanced.

items.title: Thymus: lobules, cortex, and medulla
items.description: Light-microscopy view identifying lobules, connective septa, blood vessels, darker thymic cortex, and paler medulla.
items.alt: Light-microscopy view identifying lobules, connective septa, blood vessels, darker thymic cortex, and paler medulla.

items.title: Spleen: red pulp and white pulp histology
items.description: Labeled splenic tissue showing red pulp, white-pulp nodules, capsule, trabecular vessels, and a central artery.
items.alt: Labeled splenic tissue showing red pulp, white-pulp nodules, capsule, trabecular vessels, and a central artery.

items.title: Path of blood flow through the spleen
items.description: Sequence from splenic and trabecular arterial branches through red-pulp filtration and venous return.
items.alt: Sequence from splenic and trabecular arterial branches through red-pulp filtration and venous return.

items.title: Seven nonspecific defenses: visual overview
items.description: All seven instructor-listed nonspecific defenses combined into one figure: physical barriers, phagocytes, NK surveillance, interferons, complement, inflammation, and fever.
items.alt: All seven instructor-listed nonspecific defenses combined into one figure: physical barriers, phagocytes, NK surveillance, interferons, complement, inflammation, and fever.

items.title: Natural killer cell: recognition and cytolysis
items.description: Sequence showing an NK cell contacting an abnormal cell, reorganizing its secretory apparatus, releasing cytotoxic molecules, and damaging the target.
items.alt: Sequence showing an NK cell contacting an abnormal cell, reorganizing its secretory apparatus, releasing cytotoxic molecules, and damaging the target.
items.scienceReview: The original figure emphasizes perforin; contemporary description also requires granzyme delivery and apoptosis.

items.title: Immunological escape in a growing tumor
items.description: Schematic illustrating immune surveillance and selection of tumor-cell variants that escape recognition or resist destruction.
items.alt: Schematic illustrating immune surveillance and selection of tumor-cell variants that escape recognition or resist destruction.
items.scienceReview: Simplified lecture schematic; tumor immune escape involves multiple interacting pathways.

items.title: Complement cascade and membrane attack complex
items.description: Classical complement pathway diagram highlighting antibody-dependent activation, C3b deposition, recruitment of phagocytes, and the C5b–C9 membrane attack complex.
items.alt: Classical complement pathway diagram highlighting antibody-dependent activation, C3b deposition, recruitment of phagocytes, and the C5b–C9 membrane attack complex.

items.title: Acute inflammation: coordinated local response
items.description: Diagram relating tissue injury, mast-cell mediators, increased vessel permeability, phagocyte recruitment, clotting, and tissue repair.
items.alt: Diagram relating tissue injury, mast-cell mediators, increased vessel permeability, phagocyte recruitment, clotting, and tissue repair.
items.scienceReview: A high-level sequence; not all inflammatory responses proceed in this fixed order.

items.title: Naturally versus artificially acquired immunity
items.description: Lecture classification diagram contrasting active versus passive immunity and naturally versus artificially acquired protection.
items.alt: Lecture classification diagram contrasting active versus passive immunity and naturally versus artificially acquired protection.
items.scienceReview: The slide places innate immunity under an umbrella labeled specific resistance, which is conceptually misleading. Use the article’s clearer innate/adaptive distinction.

items.title: Overview of cell-mediated and antibody-mediated immunity
items.description: Summary diagram showing how specific immunity coordinates T-cell activity and B-cell antibody responses alongside nonspecific protection.
items.alt: Summary diagram showing how specific immunity coordinates T-cell activity and B-cell antibody responses alongside nonspecific protection.

items.title: MHC class I: presenting intracellular peptides
items.description: Diagram of intracellular peptides being loaded onto class I MHC molecules and transported to the cell surface for CD8 T-cell surveillance.
items.alt: Diagram of intracellular peptides being loaded onto class I MHC molecules and transported to the cell surface for CD8 T-cell surveillance.
items.scienceReview: MHC class I presentation occurs on essentially all nucleated cells and is not itself an infection signal.

items.title: Cytotoxic T-cell activation and target-cell destruction
items.description: CD8 T-cell antigen recognition and activation followed by cytotoxic effector responses; includes memory-cell development.
items.alt: CD8 T-cell antigen recognition and activation followed by cytotoxic effector responses; includes memory-cell development.
items.scienceReview: Naive CD8 T-cell priming commonly depends on professional antigen-presenting cells; the source diagram simplifies activation and costimulation.

items.title: MHC class II: processing extracellular antigens
items.description: An antigen-presenting cell engulfing extracellular material, processing it in vesicles, and displaying peptide fragments with class II MHC.
items.alt: An antigen-presenting cell engulfing extracellular material, processing it in vesicles, and displaying peptide fragments with class II MHC.

items.title: Helper T cells and B-cell antibody production
items.description: Sequence illustrating B-cell antigen binding, helper T-cell signaling, expansion of B-cell clones, memory B cells, and antibody-secreting plasma cells.
items.alt: Sequence illustrating B-cell antigen binding, helper T-cell signaling, expansion of B-cell clones, memory B cells, and antibody-secreting plasma cells.
items.scienceReview: T-dependent B-cell activation also relies on direct co-stimulation, not cytokines alone.

items.title: Antibody molecular structure
items.description: Labeled immunoglobulin diagram identifying heavy and light chains, variable and constant regions, disulfide bonds, and antigen-binding sites.
items.alt: Labeled immunoglobulin diagram identifying heavy and light chains, variable and constant regions, disulfide bonds, and antigen-binding sites.

items.title: IgM pentamer and secretory IgA dimer
items.description: Comparison of the multimeric structures used by the IgM and secretory IgA antibody classes.
items.alt: Comparison of the multimeric structures used by the IgM and secretory IgA antibody classes.

items.title: What antibody binding actually does
items.description: Instructor figure summarizing neutralization, agglutination, opsonization, complement activation, interference with adhesion, and inflammatory effects.
items.alt: Instructor figure summarizing neutralization, agglutination, opsonization, complement activation, interference with adhesion, and inflammatory effects.

items.title: Primary versus secondary antibody responses
items.description: Comparative graphs showing the relative time courses of IgM and IgG in primary and secondary immune responses.
items.alt: Comparative graphs showing the relative time courses of IgM and IgG in primary and secondary immune responses.

items.title: Immune defense timing after bacterial infection
items.description: Relative timing of neutrophils, macrophages, NK cells, cytotoxic T cells, plasma cells, and serum antibodies during a schematic immune response.
items.alt: Relative timing of neutrophils, macrophages, NK cells, cytotoxic T cells, plasma cells, and serum antibodies during a schematic immune response.
items.scienceReview: Illustrative generalized timeline, not a universal or clinically predictive timing chart.
